indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B4.5.4.1 Know that climate change is one of the most important environmental issues facing the world today
indicator.objective: Explain that burning is one of the causes of climate change

skills.description: Recognise simply that climate change means long-term changes in weather patterns (e.g. hotter days, changed rainfall).
Explain that burning (bush burning, burning of waste, burning of fuel) is one of the causes of climate change.
Recognise that burning produces smoke which dirties the air.
State effects of burning on humans, plants, animals and property (e.g. harm to health, destruction of plants and animals, loss of property).
Predict what happens if burning of vegetation and waste continues (e.g. more smoke, dirty air, hotter environment).
Suggest simple ways to reduce burning (e.g. avoid bush burning, dispose of waste properly instead of burning).

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Burning waste is always good because it removes rubbish.
Climate change is caused only by factories, not by small fires.
Bush burning helps plants grow better.
Burning only affects the person who starts the fire.
Climate change means the weather changes from morning to evening.

options: The weather changing from morning to evening
A change in the colour of the sky
A change in the time of day
hints: Think about changes over many years.
It is not about daily weather.
questions.explanation: Climate change means long-term changes in weather patterns, such as hotter days or changes in rainfall.
questions.misconception: Climate change means the weather changes from morning to evening.

questions.stem: Which of these is a cause of climate change?
questions.explanation: Burning of waste and vegetation produces smoke that contributes to climate change.
questions.misconception: Climate change is caused only by factories.

questions.stem: What does burning produce that dirties the air?
hints: You can see it rising from a fire.
questions.explanation: Burning produces smoke, which dirties the air and can harm health.

questions.stem: What can bush burning do to plants and animals?
options: Kill them and destroy their homes
questions.explanation: Bush burning kills plants and animals and destroys their homes.
questions.misconception: Bush burning helps plants grow better.

questions.stem: Which of these helps reduce burning?
options: Disposing of waste properly in bins
questions.explanation: Disposing of waste properly in bins helps reduce burning and its harmful effects.
questions.misconception: Burning waste is always good because it removes rubbish.

questions.stem: Why is burning considered a cause of climate change?
options: It produces smoke and gases that trap heat
hints: Smoke and gases go into the air.
questions.explanation: Burning produces smoke and gases that trap heat in the atmosphere, contributing to climate change.
questions.misconception: Burning does not affect the climate.

questions.stem: Which statement about smoke from burning is correct?
options: It dirties the air and can harm health
hints: Smoke is not good to breathe.
questions.explanation: Smoke from burning dirties the air and can harm the health of people and animals.

questions.stem: A farmer sets fire to a bush. What effect can this have on the farmer's property?
options: It can destroy crops and buildings
hints: It can burn houses and farms.
questions.explanation: Bush burning can spread and destroy crops, buildings, and other property.
questions.misconception: Burning only affects the person who starts the fire.

questions.stem: What will happen if people continue to burn waste and vegetation?
options: There will be more smoke and the environment will get hotter
questions.explanation: Continuous burning will produce more smoke, dirty the air, and contribute to a hotter environment.
questions.misconception: Burning waste is harmless in the long run.

answer: changes in the weather over many years
long-term changes in the earth's weather
hints: Think about changes over a long time.
questions.explanation: Climate change is long-term change in weather patterns, like hotter days or changes in rainfall.
questions.misconception: Climate change means daily weather changes.

questions.stem: Give one reason why burning causes climate change.
answer: it produces smoke and gases that trap heat
smoke and gases from burning trap heat
it releases smoke that warms the earth
questions.explanation: Burning produces smoke and gases that trap heat in the atmosphere, leading to climate change.

questions.stem: What does burning produce that makes the air dirty?
hints: You can see it rising from a fire.
questions.explanation: Burning produces smoke, which makes the air dirty.

questions.stem: Which of these is an effect of bush burning on humans?
options: It can cause health problems from smoke
hints: Smoke is not good to breathe.
questions.explanation: Bush burning produces smoke that can cause breathing problems and other health issues.

questions.stem: A learner says, 'Burning waste is good because it removes rubbish.' What is the best correction?
options: No, burning produces smoke that harms the environment
No, burning makes the rubbish disappear completely
hints: There are better ways to manage waste.
questions.explanation: Burning waste is not good because it produces smoke that dirties the air and contributes to climate change.
questions.misconception: Burning waste is always good because it removes rubbish.

questions.stem: Suggest one way to reduce burning in your community.
answer: dispose of waste in bins instead of burning
compost food waste instead of burning
hints: Do not set fire to bushes.
questions.explanation: Ways to reduce burning include avoiding bush burning, disposing of waste in bins, and recycling or composting instead of burning.
questions.misconception: Burning waste is the only way to manage it.

questions.stem: Which of these shows an effect of burning on animals?
options: They lose their homes and can be killed
questions.explanation: Burning destroys vegetation and habitats, and can kill animals.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes climate change?
options: It is a change in weather from day to night
It is a change in the colour of the sky
It is long-term change in weather patterns over many years
It is a change in the time of sunrise each day
questions.explanation: Climate change refers to long-term changes in weather patterns over many years.
questions.misconception: Climate change means daily weather changes.

questions.stem: Explain how burning can affect humans, plants, and animals.
answer: burning produces smoke that harms human health, kills plants, and destroys animal homes
smoke from burning harms humans, fire kills plants, and destroys animals' habitats
burning harms humans through smoke, kills plants, and destroys animal habitats
questions.explanation: Burning harms humans through smoke (breathing problems), kills plants, and destroys the homes of animals.

questions.stem: Design a poster that shows the effects of burning on climate change. Include at least two effects, such as smoke and dirty air, and write a short message encouraging people to stop burning waste.

criteria.description: Showed at least two effects of burning on climate change
Used drawings to show smoke and dirty air
Included a short message encouraging people not to burn waste

hints: Include a picture of a clean environment.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
